youtube.title: How to tell marketing strategy from tactics
youtube.description:

clips.linkedin:
Give AI last year's results, your customer research and your competitors' sites, and it drafts your situation analysis.

That's the evidence a plan stands on. This clip is about the stage after it, where most plans I'm shown go wrong. A list of channels with "strategy" written at the top.

The cost is real, because a list of tactics gives you no basis for saying no to anything. The test I use is whether the line would still be true if every campaign changed. If it survives, it's strategy.

The situation analysis is the job to hand over. It comes back with three to five findings, each with its evidence, and a list of what it couldn't verify. A person still decides which findings matter.

The podcast voices are AI-generated. The full episode and the SOSTAC article are at https://manual-focus.co.uk/blog/sostac-marketing-plan-basics/
clips.text: Strategy is the route. Who you'll target, how you'll position the brand against the alternatives, which channels carry the plan. Smith makes a point I like a lot. Strategy is the shortest part of a plan and, in his experience, the weakest part of most plans. He has a checklist for it too, doesn't he? TOPPP SEED. He does, and it starts where you'd expect, with target markets and positioning. Tactics are the details of that route, the marketing mix. The test I use is whether a line would still be true if every campaign changed. "Win cyclists who train indoors through the winter, through coaches and clubs rather than paid social." That survives a change of campaign, so it's strategy.

Give AI last year's results, your customer research and your competitors' sites, and it drafts your situation analysis.

In a SOSTAC plan that's the stage that eats the most time, and it's the slog that used to make a proper situation analysis too expensive for a lot of teams.

What comes back is a draft with three to five findings, the evidence under each, and a list of what it couldn't verify. A person still decides which findings matter.

The second job is checking the plan you've already written. Paste it in and it sorts every line into the six stages, showing where tactics are sitting under strategy and which objectives have no measure.

clips.text: Get AI on this. The situation pack. That's the one that eats the most time. Give it last year's results, your customer research and a list of your main competitors' websites. Second, get AI on checking the plan you've already written. Paste in the draft and ask it to sort every line into the six stages.
